[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Count Triplets That Can Form Two Arrays of Equal XOR** [LC 1442 · Count Triplets That Can Form Two Arrays of Equal XOR](https://leetcode.com/problems/count-triplets-that-can-form-two-arrays-of-equal-xor/){difficulty="Medium"}

Three indices again, but the shape is the opposite of @sec-cnt-p4-triplets, and the reason is one line of algebra. $a$ and $b$ are the XORs of two *disjoint* halves of the same window $arr[i .. k]$, so

$$a == b \;\iff\; a \oplus b == 0 \;\iff\; arr[i] \oplus \cdots \oplus arr[k] == 0 .$$

The middle index $j$ has vanished from the predicate. Whether the window $[i, k]$ qualifies depends only on its two ends — $j$ is **free**, and the number of legal $j$ for a fixed pair $(i, k)$ is just the size of the interval $i < j \le k$, namely $k - i$. That is the whole problem: count the zero-XOR windows and weight each by its number of interior cut points. This is the contribution technique with the roles reversed from @sec-cnt-p4-triplets — there the middle was the pivot and the ends were queried; here the ends are the pivot and the middle contributes a *multiplicative* count.

Zero-XOR windows are prefix-XOR equality, exactly the @sec-pref-other trick: with $px[0] = 0$ and $px[t+1] = px[t] \oplus arr[t]$, the window $arr[i .. k]$ XORs to $0$ iff $px[i] == px[k+1]$. For the sample, $px = [0, 2, 1, 0, 6, 1]$: $px[0] = px[3]$ gives the window $[0,2]$ with $2$ choices of $j$, and $px[2] = px[5]$ gives $[2,4]$ with $2$ more — $4$ in total, matching the two pairs of triplets LeetCode lists ($(0,1,2),(0,2,2)$ and $(2,3,4),(2,4,4)$).

The last rung removes the quadratic loop too. Fix the right end $t = k+1$ with prefix value $x$; each earlier index $i$ with $px[i] == x$ contributes $k - i = (t - 1) - i$, so the charge is

$$\sum_{\substack{i < t \,:\, px[i] = x}} (t - 1 - i) \;=\; \mathrm{cnt}[x] \cdot (t-1) \;-\; \mathrm{tot}[x],$$

where $\mathrm{cnt}[x]$ is how many earlier positions carry prefix value $x$ and $\mathrm{tot}[x]$ is the **sum of those indices**. A pair of tables keyed by prefix value replaces the inner loop — the same "count and sum of the earlier ones" trick that computes $\sum_{i<j} |x_i - x_j|$ in @sec-cnt-pairsum. Watch the storyboard reach $4$ in one pass: at $t = 3$ the table says $\mathrm{cnt}[0] = 1$, $\mathrm{tot}[0] = 0$, charge $1 \cdot 2 - 0 = 2$; at $t = 5$, $\mathrm{cnt}[1] = 1$, $\mathrm{tot}[1] = 2$, charge $1 \cdot 4 - 2 = 2$.

Note the arithmetic never overflows: the answer is at most the number of triplets, $\binom{n+1}{3} = \binom{301}{3} = 4{,}499{,}950$, and XOR keeps values inside the input's bit width.

[Solved in full in @sec-cnt-p4-xortri.]{.card-link}
